ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18528, as last amended by Act No. 19889, effective November 1, 2024) and its Enforcement Decree; Crime Proceeds Concealment Regulation Act (Act No. 18621, as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee Act (Act No. 18929, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 17509, as amended), particularly Articles 289 and 292; Commercial Registration Rules; Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit Beneficial Owner Identification Guidance and AML Supervisory Manual.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Chusik Hoesa Registration Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the competent seat (e.g., Seoul Central District Court)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille Convention member state: obtain the certified court registry extract, then apply for an Apostille certificate from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs; do not add consular legalization. For a non-member state: obtain the certified extract, then arrange Republic of Korea MOFA legalization, and then submit the legalized document to the destination state's embassy or consulate in the Republic of Korea for consular legalization. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Business Registration Certificate and Corporate Existence Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille Convention member state: have the tax office-issued certificate notarized if required, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-member state: notarize if required, obtain Republic of Korea MOFA legalization, and then have the destination state's consular post in the Republic of Korea apply its consular legalization. Never chain the Apostille and consular routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing formation, name clearance filing, bank account opening, and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators/initial Board of Directors in the name of the proposed Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign the board resolution before a Korean notary public; then, for an Apostille Convention state, apply for a Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. For a non-member state, after notarization obtain Republic of Korea MOFA legalization and then destination-state embassy/consulate legalization in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jungwan) certified by a Korean notary public and filed with the registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public and the District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Approach a Korean notary for notarization of the Articles of Association; for an Apostille Convention state, obtain the Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-member state, after notarization obtain Republic of Korea MOFA legalization and then the destination state's consular legalization in the Republic of Korea. Use only one authentication route, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and account attestation from a licensed Korean bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed Korean bank such as KB Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, or Hana Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the bank reference letter on the bank's official letterhead under the bank's corporate seal; for an Apostille Convention state, have the bank officer's signature notarized if the destination requires it, then obtain the Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-member state, notarize, obtain Republic of Korea MOFA legalization, then destination-state embassy/consulate legalization. The Apostille path and consular path must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Seal Impression (Seal Impression Confirmation) for the corporate seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court registry office executing the seal registration for the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the official seal impression certificate from the registry office; for an Apostille Convention member state, apply for the Apostille from the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-member state, obtain Republic of Korea MOFA legalization and then the destination state's consular legalization in the Republic of Korea. The two authentication methods are mutually exclusive and may not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, directors, officers, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and commercial counterparties must be run against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, Republic of Korea asset-freeze notices issued under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, the Anti-Money Laundering Act list, and the European Union asset-freeze lists. Politically exposed persons, non-resident founders, and any person with a beneficial interest at or above 25 percent require enhanced due diligence, with adverse-media verification, source-of-wealth inquiry, and a written risk score. Screening must occur before name reservation, at incorporation, before bank account opening, and on an ongoing periodic basis, with all hits escalated to the designated AML compliance officer and documented for regulator inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Registry (Internet Registration Office, www.iros.go.kr) Company Name Search and the Korean Commercial Registry Information System (BizInfo); KOTRA foreign-investor support portal as supplementary guidance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act, the company name must be expressed in Hangul and must include the form suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa) for a stock corporation. A foreign-language trade name may be used only as a registered alias through phonetic transliteration, never as a substitute for the mandatory Hangul name. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive word or trade name; (2) a business-purpose descriptor corresponding to the ISIC 5820 e-sports community platform operation; (3) the corporate form suffix; and (4) an optional romanized or foreign-language alias submitted in Revised Romanization of Korean. The name must be string-identical at the registry level to the intended Hangul name, and phonetically misleadingly similar names in the same business class are barred.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Korea (when used in a manner implying a state agency or government sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the incorporator must submit a written objection to the registry judge within 14 days, attaching the name-search result, the proposed Hangul spelling, and corrected distinguishing words. If the registry judge denies the objection, the incorporator may file a permission appeal to the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 7 days; a final appeal to the Supreme Court is available within 7 days thereafter. If the rejection arises from a sensitive or prohibited token, the incorporator must obtain ministerial approval from the relevant licensing authority and simultaneously reserve a replacement name to avoid further delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mailing-only address is rejected by Korean tax authorities and banks for an online revenue-generating platform. The National Tax Service requires a determinable physical place where the representative, tax notice, and process can be received, and banks require verified physical presence for AML customer due diligence and for Stripe/PayPal settlement links. A professionally leased shared office or coworking unit may be acceptable if the company has a signed lease, the landlord's building registration certificate, dedicated work space, on-site mail handling, and actual director attendance capability; however, a single mailbox with no human presence will fail inspection and may cause bank account closure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) registered office matches the tax invoice address; (2) original lease contract and building registration certificate are present; (3) a physical signboard or platform-identifying signage is displayed; (4) at least one director or authorized employee is present during business hours; (5) computers, server logs, consumer refund capacity, and business records are physically accessible; (6) VAT filing corresponds to transaction data. Quantified risk: for a low-risk e-sports platform with a virtual-office arrangement, the probability of an unannounced district-tax-office or municipal inspection within the first 12 months is approximately 55-65 percent; a fully staffed physical office reduces this to below 10 percent in the same period.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court registration fee for incorporation of Chusik Hoesa (registration tax, local education surtax, and court filing fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registry Office and the local government under the Local Tax Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Local Tax Act Article 28 and the Court Fees Act; actual amount depends on subscribed capital and no minimum capital is required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and corporate name search certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Registry (www.iros.go.kr)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No government fee for online name search and clearance; free electronic name-search service.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association, incorporation deed, and board/POA documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Notary Public commissioned by the Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary fee tariff under the Notary Public Act; prevailing Seoul market benchmark for standard corporate formation documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the six-document corporate bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs and, for non-Apostille destinations, the destination state's embassy or consulate in the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOFA statutory Apostille fee of approximately USD 20 per document plus destination-state consular legalization fees; market benchmark for a processing agent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate AML/UBO due diligence attorney fee, PEP and sanctions screening, and Stripe/PayPal payment-rail compliance advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm or external AML compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed-fee market benchmark for Stage 1 pre-incorporation diligence in Seoul; not a statutory government tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified corporate registry extracts, certificate of good standing, and business registration certificate copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registry Office and National Tax Service district office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory court issuance fee per certified registry extract; National Tax Service business registration certificate fee is zero.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), especially Articles 288, 289, 290, 292, 293, 295, 317, 318, 329, 330, 383, 389, 393, and related Supreme Court Registration Rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filings are accepted through the Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company, together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting capital deposit and officer consent forms
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None imposed by the Commercial Act as a minimum mandatory capital; however, all issued shares must be fully subscribed and paid before registration. The paid-in amount must be held in a bank escrow account under the proposed corporate name, and a bank-issued balance certificate must be attached to the incorporation application; the funds may not be withdrawn except upon completion of registration or a court-approved refund.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CHUSIK HOESA (THE COMPANY)

(1) CONVENING. Pursuant to Article 390 and related provisions of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, the Board of Directors of the Company, duly organized with the presence of a majority of directors and at least one outside director where required, was held at the registered office on [DATE] at [TIME]. The meeting having been lawfully convened, the Chairperson of the Board confirmed quorum and declared, by unanimous consent, that the following resolutions are just, lawful and binding.

(2) SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the total authorized share capital shall be such sum as recorded in the Articles of Incorporation, divided into a fixed number of ordinary shares with a par value of at least KRW 100 per share; that the subscription of all issued shares has been duly completed by the founding shareholders; that the full subscription price has been deposited into a bank escrow account in the corporate name under formation, as evidenced by the deposit balance certificate issued by the depository bank; and that the directors are authorized to file the statutory capital contribution report with the competent Court Registry Office and to take all actions necessary to perfect corporate existence.

(3) BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that [BANK NAME] is appointed as the principal depository bank, and the Chairperson, the Chief Executive Officer and the Corporate Secretary, acting in pairs or within delegated single-signature limits, are authorized to open, operate, close and pledge accounts, issue payment orders, and negotiate instruments on behalf of the Company; provided that any transaction exceeding KRW 100,000,000 requires two authorized signatories.

(4) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [REGISTERED ADDRESS], Republic of Korea, within the territorial jurisdiction of the [DISTRICT] Court Registration Office; that this address is the principal place of business; and that the Chief Executive Officer is delegated to execute, register and renew the lease and to notify all authorities.

(5) APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Internal Director, [NAME] as Director, and [NAME] as Auditor, each to serve for the maximum term permitted by law and to hold the authorities granted by statute and the bylaws; the Representative Director is authorized to represent the Company in all legal, tax, banking and administrative matters.

(6) GOVERNANCE AND RATIFICATION. RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation, shareholders registry, stock ledger, minute book and corporate seal registration are confirmed; that share certificates are authorized for issuance; and that all pre-incorporation contracts made for the benefit of the Company are ratified. The Representative Director and Corporate Secretary are directed to file this resolution with the Court Registry, National Tax Service, local municipal authorities and banks, and to pay all filing taxes. This resolution is adopted unanimously and is effective as of the date above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit at least one proposed company name together with an English transliteration through the Internet Registration Office portal. The system checks exact and probable similarity against existing registered entities. Upon approval, preserve the reservation receipt. Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, ensuring that the corporate purpose expressly covers software publishing, esports tournament administration, online game matchmaking, community platform operation and ancillary services. Have the draft reviewed by a licensed Korean attorney before notarization. If a foreign incorporator acts through counsel, include a notarized power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport or national identity document of each incorporator
Notarized power of attorney if filed by a representative
Memorandum containing three proposed corporate names
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean legal form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, select the next reserved name and resubmit within the same session. If the portal raises a query, correct the company-purpose statement and refile; if the reservation expires, request one administrative renewal before returning to step one.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank and Notary Public duly commissioned under Korean notarial law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow deposit account at a licensed bank using the pre-approved corporate name and have each subscriber transmit the agreed subscription price. Obtain the bank-issued balance certificate evidencing that the full deposit is held. Deliver the final Articles of Incorporation to a notary public qualified in the Republic of Korea. The notary verifies the identities of the incorporators, the legality of the corporate clauses, the subscription statements and the escrow certificate. Once satisfied, the notary affixes the attestation and returns the certified original. Invite counsel to conduct a closing review before the court filing and preserve every receipt as evidence for the registrar.
required_dossiers: Final draft of Articles of Incorporation
Subscription statements from all incorporators
Share subscription payment receipt and escrow balance certificate
Passport copies and alien registration cards of all subscribers
Power of attorney for notarization if represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency note, amend the Articles with unanimous incorporator consent and re-notarize as the final version. If the bank refuses to issue the balance certificate, correct the account title to match the approved corporate name, present the notarized power of attorney, and require reissuance before the registration window closes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registry Filing for Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, acting through the Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Internet Registration Office and file the application for registration of incorporation under the district court that has territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. Attach all dossiers electronically, pay the registration license tax and court fee, and acknowledge the filing number. The registrar will review statutory compliance, including the accuracy of the share subscription, the bank balance certificate, the officer acceptances and the registered-office address. If complete, the court issues the certificate of incorporation and corporate registration number. Verify that the property lease and the Articles of Incorporation match the exact address and that the statutory representative's consent is signed.
required_dossiers: Certified true copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application for registration of incorporation
Bank balance certificate of paid-in capital
Report of incorporators and directors as to subscription and capital payment
Acceptance declarations of each director and auditor
Certificate of lease or title deed for registered office
Corporate seal impression card if requested
Power of attorney to the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court transmits a correction order, respond through the Internet Registration Office within the statutory grace period and upload the supplemental evidence. If the filing is suspended because of underpaid registration tax, pay the difference with the applicable surcharge and resubmit. If refusal persists, file a written appeal or a fresh application with comprehensive curative evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Statutory Book Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of Chusik Hoesa (internal corporate governance organ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the certificate is issued, convene the first board meeting at the registered office or by unanimous written consent if the Articles permit. Adopt the formal first board resolution in the exact form recorded in this dossier, covering paid-in capital, banking signatories, registered-office adoption and statutory officer appointments. Establish the corporate seal, minute book, share ledger, shareholders registry and statutory books. Issue share certificates and obtain signed acceptance confirmations from each director and auditor. If a bank requires an electronic board-resolution validation, deliver a certified extract of the minutes together with the authorized signatory list.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Minutes of share subscription audit or capital payment report
Draft first board resolution
Shareholder list with subscribed shares
Corporate seal registration application and seal impression
Bank account signatory forms if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum challenge occurs, hold an adjourned meeting under the Commercial Act or obtain the unanimous written consent of all directors. If the corporate seal registration is refused, correct the seal impression and submit the official identification card of the representative director with a revised application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Tax Setup and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Office / Hometax System and licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of incorporation, file the business registration application with the National Tax Service through the Hometax portal or at the district tax office. Select business code 5820 and complete value-added-tax registration. Submit the certificate of incorporation, the lease agreement, the representative's identification, and the corporate seal. Once approved, obtain the corporate business registration certificate and open operational bank accounts using the certificate, the first board resolution and a corporate bank mandate. Register employees with the national pension, health insurance, employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance schemes as hiring occurs.
required_dossiers: Business registration application
Certificate of incorporation copy
Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution certified copy
Registered office lease agreement
Representative director's identification
Bank opening documents and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office returns the business-registration application, rectify the address or representative documents and resubmit through Hometax within seven days. If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide a beneficial-ownership declaration, explain the tournament fee payment flows, and produce a source-of-funds statement for the paid-in capital.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the undertaking is a pure digital software publisher and esports community platform under ISIC 5820; it does not operate a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing plant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit is triggered by the registered business scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable to this digital undertaking; for reference, environmental impact assessment administration in the Republic of Korea is carried out by the Ministry of Environment and relevant local governments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - digital software publishing and esports community platform services do not appear on the positive project-type list of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no full EIA report, prior environmental review, or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero process wastewater discharge, zero regulated VOC process emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation. Ordinary office waste will be managed through licensed municipal waste collection; any cloud or data-center servers are owned and operated by the hosting provider under separate environmental and e-waste compliance obligations. Office water use and electricity consumption do not trigger quantitative EIA thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to civil-defense or manufacturing fire permits because there is no physical manufacturing or warehouse operation. However, the leased office must comply with the Fire Safety Act by maintaining fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, and a fire protection plan, and must undergo the applicable fire-fighting facility self-inspection. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Company must register for industrial accident compensation insurance and conduct a basic office risk assessment. No structural load inspection or chemical storage clearance is required for a software-only office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); customs clearance via Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) must file the Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office within 20 days of business commencement, attaching the certificate of incorporation, registered articles of incorporation, and representative identity documentation; the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which also serves as the legal entity VAT identification number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a domestic place of business, the entity must register with the NTS through a domestically appointed tax representative no later than 20 days after commencing taxable supply, filing the same Business Registration Application together with the power of attorney, constitutional documents, board resolution authorizing the tax representative, and an address of service in Korea; the NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number in the name of the non-resident enterprise. There is no separate VAT ID in Korea; the Business Registration Number is the sole statutory TIN/VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Republic of Korea does not maintain a check-the-box election; hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed prescriptively under the Controlled Foreign Company rules and tax treaty substance provisions, not through entity classification elections)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident corporations: mandatory registration from business commencement, no turnover threshold. Non-resident enterprises: mandatory registration within 20 days of commencing taxable supplies in the Republic of Korea, no turnover exemption threshold. Individual simplified taxpayer threshold (KRW 80 million per annum) is not available to corporate entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoicing through the National Tax Service HomeTax system: every VAT-registered business must issue an electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) for all B2B taxable supplies and transmit it to HomeTax by the statutory deadline, generally by the 10th day of the month following the supply month. The NTS provides tax invoice transmission APIs and ERP integration; there is no real-time fiscal stamping clearance comparable to Latin American anti-fraud stamping systems, but electronic invoice data is validated and stored in the NTS tax clearance database for continuous tax monitoring.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export of goods: the goods must be physically dispatched from Korea under an export declaration cleared by Korea Customs Service; the purchaser must be a non-resident and ownership and risk must pass offshore. Zero-rated export of qualifying services, including esports platform and tournament services: the services must be supplied to a non-resident party for consumption wholly outside Korea, and if required by statutes, paid in foreign currency and covered by a written export contract. The 0% VAT rate applies only when the prescribed evidentiary documents are retained and filed with the National Tax Service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic Export Declaration bearing the exporter business registration number and customs clearance number
Commercial invoice signed by the exporter referencing the export declaration number
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the physical export movement from Korea to the foreign destination
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank confirming the inward remittance of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the National Tax Service determines that the zero-rated export substantiation is incomplete, false, or that export proceeds were not repatriated within 180 days without a legally recognized excuse, the supply is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply and VAT at 10% is assessed retrospectively. Additional penalty taxes are imposed for non-issuance or wrongful issuance of tax invoices and misdeclaration, typically 10-30% of unpaid VAT and up to 40% for intentional concealment. Criminal prosecution may follow for fraudulent export declaration or fraudulent VAT refunds, with fines and imprisonment under the Value-Added Tax Act, Customs Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the zero-rate benefit is clawed back and the exporter must file a revised tax return with penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), as monetary authority, acting together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is highly convertible on current account transactions, including service fees, royalties, payroll, and dividends, subject only to statutorily mandated reporting and genuine underlying transaction documentation. Capital account transactions remain event-driven and require prior or concurrent reporting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in authorized foreign currency deposit accounts, provided proceeds are collected within the prescribed settlement period and reported through FEIS. Profit remittance is legally possible after the foreign investment report has been completed and the capital verification certificate is issued, but the remitting bank will require proof of distributable retained earnings, audited financial statements, a board dividend resolution, tax clearance for the 20 percent (or treaty-reduced) dividend withholding tax, and a true copy of the foreign investment report certificate. Practical hurdles include lengthy documentation review, the need for an in-person banking signatory, and operation of an internal FX transaction monitoring framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, a resident exporter of goods must collect the full invoice value within 18 months from the date of export declaration; for services and digital content (including esports platform subscriptions and tournament management fees), the standard collection period is 6 months from the completion date of the service, extendable by prior approval for justified cases. No fixed mandatory conversion percentage applies; the exporter may retain 100% of foreign currency proceeds in a foreign currency deposit at an authorized foreign exchange bank. However, any transfer or payment in Korean won must be supported by an FX contract at the deposit-taking bank and reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Export proceeds that are not collected or reported on time are treated as unrepatriated export proceeds and can trigger customs, banking, and tax sanctions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd. (KB Kookmin Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Dedicated Won Account) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD/EUR multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account with Foreign Currency Settlement
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account with dedicated FEIS reporting line
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account supported by trade finance desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for use as a primary treasury or bank account; Medium only as an auxiliary card-issuing or merchant acquiring rail. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only licensed electronic financial business operators registered with the Financial Services Commission can provide payment services for Korean entities. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, and Airwallex do not have depository licenses in Korea and cannot issue Korean settlement accounts or handle won-denominated deposits. Stripe and PayPal can be used as front-end collection rails for the esports platform after the Korean entity obtains a domestic merchant or payment gateway arrangement, but all settlement funds must eventually clear into a domestic Tier-1 bank account. The treasury should therefore rely on Tier-1 banks for liquidity and treat PayPal and Stripe only as originating channels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a new Chusik Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, the representative director or a designated attorney-in-fact with a notarized power-of-attorney must physically visit the Korean branch for an in-person KYC interview; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as the sole route. The beneficial owner and the person with control, including at least one signatory, must present or provide certified copies that are apostilled or legalized under the Hague Apostille Convention. Some banks allow a professional introducer or an existing high-grade customer relationship to support the application, but physical signatory verification remains the legal and operational baseline for a foreign-owned Korean stock corporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO and nominee shareholder arrangement in the Chusik Hoesa shareholder registry; mismatch between the jurisdiction of incorporation of the parent entity and the actual controllers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an apostilled corporate registry certificate of the shareholder, current register of members, a signed UBO declaration with an ownership diagram, passport copies of each director and every 25 percent or greater shareholder, supporting bank references from the parent's home jurisdiction, and a sworn statement that no nominee or trust arrangement conceals the beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border micro-payments related to esports entry fees, prize pools, and in-game digital assets, which can be abused for layering or integration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a player and vendor KYC policy, tournament rules, prize payout logic, source of funds evidence for high-value prize payments, granular game transaction logs, sanctions and PEP screening outputs, monitoring thresholds for unusual activity, and an independent cyber or AML assessment of the platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unreported or mistimed foreign exchange transactions: capital account inflow received before FDI report approval, or outbound remittances split to avoid FEIS reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce the completed Foreign Investment Report and Certificate issued through KOTRA or the designated bank, all FEIS transaction receipts, board-approved loan or share agreements, bank FX application forms, and underlying commercial contracts with tax invoices; the treasurer must certify that each remittance uses the correct purpose code and that no transaction-splitting occurs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance and board authority for the Korean entity, where the business model is treated as a pass-through or aggregator for foreign controllers, causing the bank to suspect the Chusik Hoesa is not a genuine operating company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the corporate articles of incorporation, headquarters lease agreement, payroll and social-insurance records for employees in Korea, minutes of board meetings approving major agreements, tax filings and tax clearance certificates, an operating expenditure budget, and a business plan showing 12-month projections for esports platform operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must submit a prior foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank. Upon acceptance, the investor opens a dedicated foreign investment capital escrow account with the reporting Tier-1 bank, remits the equity amount through an authenticated SWIFT or international wire using the FEIS purpose code for direct equity investment, and the bank verifies the remittance against the reported amount and FX contract. After the Chusik Hoesa files the share subscription and payment report and issues shares, capital verification is completed by an external Korean CPA using the foreign investment report certificate, the escrow account statement, the board resolution on share issuance, and the paid-in share capital ledger entry. The subscribed capital is then released into the operational currency account for business use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for standard low-documentation payments such as royalty payments, licensing fees, supplier invoices, and cross-border prize remittances to tournament winners, always with a tax invoice and FEIS reporting. Use Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) only for physical imports of servers, tournament hardware, or broadcast equipment when seller financing risk exists. Documentary collections (MT400 or MT410) are available but rarely used for an esports platform and should be reserved for the purchase of bulky capital equipment where the bank will hold shipping documents. All outbound payments to non-residents require tax withholding whether classified as dividend, royalty, or technical service fee, and must not be made to sanctioned countries or blocked parties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward contracts for KRW/USD, KRW/EUR and KRW/JPY are permissible when the platform has a genuine forecasted receivable or payable under a valid commercial agreement; maturity cannot exceed 12 months without special approval.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only via an authorized foreign exchange bank for underlying Korean won exposures where the counterparty cannot execute a deliverable forward, and the transaction must be included in the bank's FEIS reporting; speculative NDF positions are prohibited for a non-financial corporate.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps are permissible only when the Chusik Hoesa has outstanding foreign-currency borrowings or multi-currency operating leases and the hedge is used to fix or reduce FX risk, not to create an arbitrage position; the bank will require a board resolution, underlying loan documents, and periodic mark-to-market collateral if any.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate secretarial register audit and statutory-register inspection certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company board and appointed corporate secretary/registered agent; registers must be available for inspection at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 of each fiscal year or, if the fiscal year is not calendar, no later than the last day of the third month after the fiscal year end; register audit to be completed before filing the corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient or inaccessible statutory registers may attract administrative fines under the Commercial Act and evidence/civil-penalty risk; repeated refusal to permit inspection can support a court petition for director removal or dissolution in serious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; minutes retained in the statutory minute book; no government filing required unless director changes are separately registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year, the deadline is March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual general meeting may result in a court-ordered meeting and administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000; directors may be removed by court order; prolonged governance failure may be ground for court dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA audit report and audited financial statements (required if statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service DART system and the National Tax Service attached to the corporate tax return; audit report to the board and shareholders before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and the audit report tabled at the AGM held within 3 months of fiscal year end; audited financial statements accompany the corporate tax return due within the same 3-month window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a registered Korean CPA auditor or file the audit report may trigger FSS sanctions, administrative penalties up to KRW 50,000,000 under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, and possible designation of a substitute auditor by the authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Tax Final Return with self-assessed tax and tax base computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax equal to 20% of unpaid or underreported corporate income tax, 40% for false returns, plus statutory late-payment interest; continued non-filing leads to enforced collection and asset seizure and may ultimately support court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax return for corporate income (inhabitant/surtax layer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local taxing authority (si/gun/gu) through WeTax e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the month following the corporate income tax filing deadline; for a calendar-year company, April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of underreported or unpaid local income tax, 40% for fraudulent non-filing, plus daily late-payment interest; enforcement can include collection of local taxes from bank accounts and business assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax returns for semi-annual VAT periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half January-June: July 25; second half July-December: January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported or underpaid VAT carries additional tax of 10% plus late-payment interest; invoice-media violations add separate penalties; the NTS may revoke the business registration if the company is habitually non-compliant or fails to maintain taxable business activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll and withholding tax returns for employee income tax and resident local income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax and local taxing authority via WeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 10th day of the month following the month in which wages or other withholdable amounts were paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding default is punishable by additional tax of 3% or more of the unwithheld amount and repayment obligations; late filing and late payment penalties accumulate daily, and personal liability of the representative director may arise.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry amendment for re-election of directors and changes in registered company matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry at the local District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the relevant event; for Chusik Hoesa directors with the statutory maximum 3-year term, this occurs at each re-election following the AGM and upon any change of registered matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted registration is punishable by administrative fines under the Commercial Registration Act and Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, typically up to KRW 5,000,000; unregistered director changes are not effective against third parties acting in good faith.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-investment status report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy via the Korea Foreign Direct Investment System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report due by February 15 following the fiscal year end if the company has any foreign-invested enterprise status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign-investment report may trigger fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and adverse treatment for future foreign investment support, protection, and exchange controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Publication of final balance sheet or financial summary for large stock companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public disclosure requirement under the Korean Commercial Act; no receipting agency if publication is posted on the company website or in an official gazette; if a registered listed issuer, also submitted to FSS DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the annual shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-publication by a large Chusik Hoesa is an administrative-offense ground under the Commercial Act and can give rise to fines; creditors and shareholders may also compel disclosure through court proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Korean Chusik Hoesa must obtain a mandatory independent certified audit from a licensed Korean CPA firm if: (i) it is listed on a Korean stock exchange; (ii) its total assets reflected in the balance sheet at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9.2 million; (iii) it is designated as a public-interest or special-category company by the Financial Services Commission or Financial Supervisory Service; or (iv) it falls under financial-industry audit rules under other specific statutes. For an ordinary unlisted esports-community platform, there is no standalone turnover-only or headcount-only statutory audit trigger under the external-audit law; a company with total assets below KRW 12 billion and no designation or listing is generally exempt from mandatory independent external audit. However, if the company's articles of incorporation, shareholders, bank financing arrangements, or licensing counterparties require a certified audit, the engagement must still be performed in accordance with the Korean Statement on Auditing Standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, fully aligned with IFRS) for stock companies that are listed, and for non-listed companies that choose K-IFRS; non-listed companies subject to external audit may alternatively apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles); small companies below the external-audit threshold may apply simplified SME accounting standards or tax-basis accounting for corporate tax return purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently maintain a standalone annual beneficial-ownership filing regime for a private Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is evidenced through the register of shareholders maintained at the company's registered office, and a shareholder must be registered in that ledger or otherwise prove share-transfer notification to the company to exercise full corporate rights. For AML/KYC and corporate-secretarial best practice, the company must obtain an annual UBO declaration from every shareholder at each fiscal-year end, reconcile the declaration against the register of shareholders, and treat any mismatch as a material corporate-governance exception. In addition, if the company is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any change of foreign investor status or shareholding must be reported to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of the change, and an annual foreign-investment status report must be filed by February 15. The company's corporate secretary and registered agent are required to enforce the annual confirmation process and preserve the signed declarations for at least 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Register of Shareholders
Register of Directors (and auditor/audit committee members)
Register of Charges/Mortgages and security interests over company assets, if any

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 1,500 per annum for a registered office and corporate secretarial service in South Korea; USD 600 - 2,500 per annum for a licensed Seoul-based corporate agent providing English-language compliance, mailbox, and registered-office services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if fully exempt from mandatory external audit; USD 8,000 - 45,000 for a small or mid-size Chusik Hoesa with a material esports-platform revenue base that crosses the KRW 12 billion asset or other audit trigger; larger or public-interest companies will exceed USD 50,000 depending on subsidiary scope, transaction volume, and internal-control testing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on the first KRW 200,000,000 of taxable income; 19% on income above KRW 200,000,000; 21% on income above KRW 20,000,000,000; 24% on income above KRW 300,000,000,000, plus a 10% local surtax on national corporate income tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean Free Economic Zone and foreign-invested enterprise tax holidays, R&D and high-tech facility investment tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, job creation tax credits, SME preferential rates, and targeted technology-transfer/patent income incentives; no general patent box

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement (Corporate Tax Act Article 60(1)), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal, with accompanying financial statements, tax reconciliation statement, the Report on International Transactions, and the Transfer Pricing Local File/Master File when statutory thresholds are exceeded
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, supplemented by interim estimated corporate tax payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the return is due by March 31; a one-month filing extension may be available for externally audited corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation identification, registration number, fiscal year begin date, fiscal year end date, business status, and legal form of the Chusik Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean corporate registration number and confirm the tax year. The domestic Korean corporation is the taxpayer; non-resident shareholders are not separately filing this return. The corporation must separately flag non-resident ownership in the shareholder register for dividend withholding compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and Korean standard industrial classification code, including the esports community platform and competitive gaming matchmaking operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Code 5820 software publishing classification and describe the platform as online gaming, tournament/matchmaking services, and digital content distribution. Cross-border payment settlement through Stripe or PayPal must not cause the platform to be presented merely as an offshore payment conduit; Korean-source revenue from Korean users remains fully reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, net revenue, and taxable gross sales from entry fees, tournament tickets, in-game purchases, subscriptions, advertising, sponsorship, and platform commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue on an accrual basis and include all sales settled through Stripe, PayPal, or any offshore PSP. Do not omit revenue because settlement is received in a foreign bank account. Non-resident investors cannot use offshore collecting agents to exclude Korean-source turnover from the corporate tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, cost of sales, general and administrative expenses, depreciation, and tax adjustments including non-deductible items and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees, royalties, management fees, and interest paid to foreign related parties must be arm's length, supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, and matched by real economic substance. Expense deductions will be denied if the payment is to a shell or fails the beneficial ownership, substance, and documentation tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation, loss carryforward application, statutory progressive corporate tax computation, and the final national corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean Chusik Hoesa is taxed on its worldwide income as a resident corporation. Non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation here, but the corporation must trace dividends, deemed dividends, and residual income attributable to non-residents for later withholding tax obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, interim tax prepayments, withheld taxes at source, and other payments already made against the final corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available in accordance with the Corporate Tax Act only for foreign-source income actually taxed abroad. The domestic corporation may not credit Korean dividend withholding tax that will be later withheld from non-resident shareholders; that is a shareholder-level obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party transaction schedule, transfer pricing disclosure, and mandatory report on cross-border transactions with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all intercompany loans, royalty payments, software licensing, service fees, cloud infrastructure payments, and any recharging of costs to or from the non-resident shareholders. If the annual aggregate cross-border related-party transaction value exceeds KRW 5,000,000,000, the Local File is triggered; the Master File is triggered at higher thresholds. Failure to disclose creates a presumption that the transaction was not at arm's length.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and unfaithful returns attract additional tax of 10% to 20% of the underreported or unpaid corporate tax under Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus statutory overdue interest on the unpaid tax. Fraudulent tax evasion is separately prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to five times the tax evaded; aggravated evasion above large statutory amounts can increase imprisonment to up to ten years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on gross outbound cash and constructive dividends to non-resident shareholders, composed of a 20% national withholding tax plus a 2% local income tax surcharge; applicable treaty rates can reduce the dividend rate to 5% to 15% depending on shareholding and the treaty counterparty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must supply the Korean withholding agent with a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership certificate/declaration, evidence of share ownership for dividend rate reduction, and the specific tax treaty article relied upon. The Korean payer must submit the application for withholding tax reduction/exemption under the tax treaty through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal at the time of remittance. If the documentation is incomplete, the payer must withhold at the statutory 22% rate and the non-resident must seek a refund by filing with the National Tax Service. The beneficial owner must be the actual recipient, must not be a conduit, and must have substantive commercial substance in the treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for software licenses, trademarks, know-how, and platform technology are subject to the same 22% statutory withholding rate, while treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 10% or 15%. Interest paid on intercompany debt to non-resident shareholders is also subject to a statutory 22% rate, with treaty relief usually reducing interest withholding to 10%, and sometimes to zero where the treaty and beneficial ownership conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 imposes a substance-over-form doctrine, and the Corporate Tax Act and tax treaties require beneficial ownership and real business substance. The National Tax Service may disregard a Chusik Hoesa or an intercompany transaction that lacks valid commercial purpose, actual employees, premises, board decision-making, and core income-generating activities. The OECD Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) concept is used in transfer pricing and permanent establishment analyses to allocate profit to the jurisdiction where substantive personnel and strategic decisions are located.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion and Revenue Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directing the esports platform to route tournament fees, in-game purchases, and subscription revenue through foreign Stripe or PayPal accounts controlled by non-resident shareholders while excluding the revenue from the Korean corporate tax return, or fabricating deductible expenses through offshore shell vendors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax of 10% to 20% of the unpaid tax under Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, statutory overdue interest, and criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3, which allows imprisonment for up to five years and fines of up to five times the evaded tax; aggravated tax evasion above the statutory threshold can result in imprisonment for three to ten years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil where the Chusik Hoesa is a sham or the director personally directed the evasion, making the director jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and interest. Director personal assets may be seized, the director may be blacklisted as a serious tax offender with public disclosure, a travel ban may be imposed under tax collection procedures, and the director faces criminal imprisonment for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated royalties, management fees, interest, or software licensing fees to a non-resident related company without arm's length analysis, without a Transfer Pricing Local File or Master File, and without a prepared Report on International Transactions, while the Korean company retains no profit because all economic substance and strategic control have been shifted offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may adjust the taxable income under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs Article 4 and assess the difference plus additional tax and overdue interest. Failure to produce transfer pricing documentation can result in administrative penalty surcharges, denial of deductions, and a recharacterization of the excessive payments as deemed dividends or other taxable distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the non-arm's length intercompany arrangements can be held jointly and severally liable for the resulting corporate tax deficiency if the arrangements are found to be artificial and intended to evade tax. Civil asset restitution can be enforced against director personal property, the directors can be placed on the National Tax Service serious-tax-offender blacklist with travel restrictions, and criminal prosecution may follow if false documents or fraudulent transfer pricing records are submitted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Double Tax Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders through a shell entity in a low-tax jurisdiction, claiming Double Tax Agreement relief with forged or absent Tax Residency Certificates, or failing to withhold the statutory 22% on outbound payments and then colluding with the recipient to hide the distribution from the National Tax Service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Article 98 makes the Korean payer a statutory withholding agent; failure to withhold and remit makes the company liable for the uncollected tax, additional tax, and interest. False claims of treaty benefits are treated as fraudulent withholding tax under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and can attract criminal penalties including imprisonment, fine, and forfeiture of the economic benefit obtained from the under-withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director officers of the Chusik Hoesa who direct the dividend distribution or approve the treaty relief application are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties. The National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil where the payment structure is a sham, seize the director's personal property, impose an international travel ban, blacklist the director for repeat tax offenses, and pursue criminal imprisonment for intentional evasion of withholding obligations.
